headline: High-risk filesystem and shell-capable orchestration paired with document processing creates default prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read and write files and uses stdin/stdout plus tool calls; marker is a document-processing agent with no isolation or provenance controls shown. A shared workspace or manual handoff could let attacker-controlled document text influence AutoGen’s instructions, while marker may preserve or transform that content. The pathway exists, but the profiles do not prove a default shared channel.
conditions: IF AutoGen and marker exchange documents through a shared workspace or copy-paste bridge
IF marker output is fed back into AutoGen as trusted instructions
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Strip instructions from document text before passing to AutoGen
Require human review of marker output before reuse
Disable automatic re-ingestion of generated documents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and can read/write files with broad network egress; marker is document-processing with no stated filesystem or network protections. If both are pointed at the same workspace, sensitive document contents can flow from marker into AutoGen outputs or outbound model calls. The profiles do not show a guaranteed leak, but the shared-data pathway is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF both agents are configured on the same working directory
IF marker processes sensitive documents that AutoGen later forwards to a model provider
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Redact secrets before AutoGen sees documents
Limit AutoGen network egress to approved endpoints
Review outbound prompts for embedded document text
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has filesystem write and shell execution, while marker has no write, shell, or network capabilities listed. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable-resource writes or locking conflicts, so direct capability contention is limited. Any conflict would require unusual orchestration beyond the profiles shown.
conditions: IF marker is wrapped with additional write or shell permissions not shown in its profile
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory and AutoGen edits files there
mitigations: Keep marker read-only
Assign AutoGen a separate output directory
Avoid concurrent writes to shared files
Use file locks for any shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code, files, or instructions that marker may consume as document input, and marker’s profile shows no verification or critique step. If marker renders or forwards AutoGen output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream documents or actions. The interaction is plausible in default multi-agent workflows, though not proven to be automatic.
conditions: IF marker consumes AutoGen output without validation
IF AutoGen-produced text is treated as source-of-truth for document generation
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require citations or checksums on AutoGen outputs
Have a human approve high-impact outputs
Compare marker output against source documents
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and marker touches no data classes in the profile. AutoGen does handle application data and model-provider API keys, so compliance risk is limited to whatever data the operator routes through it. Because the other agent has no stated compliance surface, only a small documented-gap risk remains.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through AutoGen into a non-compliant model provider
IF the operator relies on marker for retention or deletion handling that is not documented
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to AutoGen
Confirm provider retention settings
Keep marker inputs free of regulated data
Document deletion/export procedures
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
